newsitem.title: USA: Hilton says HFS role in ITT bid looks same. [CORRECTED 22:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Hilton says HFS role in ITT bid looks same. [CORRECTED 22:25 GMT]

text.p: A spokesman for Hilton Hotels Corp said HFS Inc's $11 billion merger pact with CUC International "does not appear" to alter HFS's role in Hilton's $55-per-share, hostile bid for ITT Corp.
Under an agreement between Hilton and HFS, Hilton, if it acquires ITT, will license the Sheraton name to HFS.
(Corrects to clarify that HFS would license the Sheraton name, but deletes reference to HFS operating ITT's hotels if bid succeeds).
The Hilton spokeman declined to elaborate on the potential impact, if any, HFS's merger with CUC could have on the ITT takeover, which was launched four months ago.
HFS spokesmen were not immediately available to comment.

After Tuesday's market close, CUC and HFS said they will merge in a $11 billion stock swap, bringing together's HFS's widely-recognized travel and real estate franchises with CUC direct marketing and 68 million members.
HFS's franchised brands include Avis car rental, Days Inn, Super 8, Howard Johnson's, Ramada, Century 21 and Coldwell Banker.

CUC's members have access to various goods and services including travel, insurance, dining. The company owns the Welcome Wagon business and is also engaged in the creation of interactive multimedia computer software, among other operations.
